papers.title: Marginal bunching for \textit{in situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability
papers.abstract: We propose an \textit{in situ} method for certifying the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in generic linear interferometers. For particles occupying distinct input ports, the method uses two-particle marginal bunching or anti-bunching probabilities to bound full multiparticle indistinguishability through Aldous' spectral gap theorem. For Haar-random unitary interferometers, the number of experimental runs required to estimate this bound to a prescribed precision, at fixed confidence, is polynomial in the particle number, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability over the choice of interferometer. Losses are incorporated without conditioning on particle survival. The method is particularly suited to certifying photon indistinguishability in large-scale interference experiments, including Boson Sampling experiments targeting quantum computational advantage.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: Magnetic field detection is of great significance in modern fields such as medical diagnostics, geological exploration, inertial navigation, and space physics. We have previously investigated the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate. Building on these results, here we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient detection by establishing a quantitative relationship between the condensate's rotational deflection angle and the magnetic-field gradient. In this work, we present the parameter dependence of this scheme and perform a systematic optimization. We introduce a Bayesian optimization algorithm to automatically and efficiently search for the optimal combination of key parameters, thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity of the magnetic field gradient measurement. The results show that the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. This work not only provides a new approach for magnetic field gradient measurement but also serves as a reference for machine learning-empowered quantum precision measurement.

papers.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
papers.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2\pi$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.

papers.title: Ultracold polar molecules for quantum science and technology
papers.abstract: Ultracold polar molecules present a rich platform for experimental quantum science leveraging their unique properties. Of particular relevance is the intrinsic electric dipole moment of the molecule, which results in strong coupling to microwave fields and can be used to engineer long-range, anisotropic, and tunable dipole-dipole interactions. Such interactions can generate entanglement between molecules and enable the study of novel quantum many-body phenomena in parameter regimes inaccessible in other systems. Modern experiments in optical tweezers and optical lattices have demonstrated controlled interactions between molecules in coherent quantum states, and recently bulk gases of molecules have been cooled to quantum degeneracy. Motivated by these landmark advances, we present this article to explain many of the key concepts relevant to current research in the field.

papers.title: Observation of s-p Coupling in Ultralong-Range Rydberg Molecules
papers.abstract: Ultralong-range Rydberg molecules, formed by the interaction between a highly excited Rydberg atom and a ground-state atom, provide a unique platform for exploring quantum phenomena spanning nanometer- to micrometer distances as well as exotic few-body interactions. The molecular binding arises from electron-atom scattering, which is conventionally described by an independent s- and p-wave channels picture. Here we report the experimental observation of s-p coupling in Rb(nS)-Rb(5S) ultralong-range Rydberg molecules via high-resolution photoassociation spectroscopy. By varying the principal quantum number n from 31 to 36, we resolve an avoided crossing between the s- and p-wave molecular states: whenever a vibrational level bound by the p-wave well approaches one bound by the s-wave well in energy, the two states are mixed by the off-diagonal coupling U_sp, and the shifted s-wave level is identified, which is consistent with theoretical predictions. This mixing is most pronounced for low-node p-wave molecules, whose binding energies lie closer to those of the s-wave molecules. The resulting level repulsion and redistribution of spectral intensity reveal the mixed s-p character of ultralong-range Rydberg molecules and provide a more precise molecular spectroscopy.

papers.title: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation
papers.abstract: An important physical quantity that is part of the Saha ionisation equation is the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. An immense uncertainty is caused by the divergency of the neutral atom partition function arising due to the fast growing degeneracy factor of its excited n-state. We suggested a regularisation and renormalisation procedure for the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. The renormalised partition function is well defined and allows to calculate the population of the energy levels and the ionisation state of the hydrogen plasma as a function of its temperature and pressure. In the low-temperature limit the behaviour of these functions smoothly transforms to the Saha equation, which is used in the description of the low-temperature plasma. At higher temperatures the renormalised ionisation equation describes the deviation from the Saha equation. The application of the renormalised ionisation equation to the solar core and atmosphere is considered.

papers.title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates
papers.abstract: Many processes in chemistry and physics, such as autoionization, photoionization, or electron-impact collisions, involve unbound electrons. Despite their importance, theoretical methods for modeling continuum electrons remain significantly less developed than those for purely bound electronic states. Here we present a novel approach for treating continuum electrons within Gaussian-based quantum chemistry. The method represents continuum orbital in a discrete basis of standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs), where the continuum wave function is obtained by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with proper boundary conditions using an analytical representation of the Green's function in an auxiliary GTO basis set. The resulting continuum orbital is multicentered and multichannel, providing a rigorous description of scattering states. As an initial application of the new methodology, we compute Auger decay rates for several atomic and molecular systems, including Ne, H$_2$O, CO$_2$, and Ar. We demonstrate a consistent improvement of the results with increasing the quality of the continuum representation. We show also that higher-order electron-correlation effects in the bound domain are essential for an accurate treatment of satellite transitions. The present formalism therefore provides a systematically improvable Gaussian-based framework for continuum-electron problems that is fully compatible with standard quantum chemistry methods.

papers.title: Design of a radio-frequency photoinjector for generating relativistic vortex electron beams
papers.abstract: We present the design and an analysis of the classical and quantum beam dynamics for an S-band radio-frequency (RF) photoinjector dedicated to the generation of relativistic vortex electron beams carrying a quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). The field-map-based tracking simulations were performed in the ultra-low bunch charge regime ($Q = 0.63$ pC), where space-charge effects are strongly suppressed. We demonstrate that optimizing the injection phase and solenoidal focusing preserves the intrinsic thermal limit of the photoemission source, yielding a stable, emittance-compensated beam with a final kinetic energy of 4.9 MeV and a normalized transverse emittance of $56\,\pi\,\mu\mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{mrad}$. Furthermore, our quantum-mechanical analysis of single-electron Laguerre-Gaussian wave packets inside the designed accelerating fields reveals that rapid energy gain suppresses transverse quantum spreading by nearly three orders of magnitude compared to free-space propagation. This suppression protects the characteristic OAM-dependent spatial structure of the wave packet. These results establish the beam-dynamics operating regime and vacuum conditions required for subsequent experiments on the generation and transport of relativistic vortex electron beams.
